title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is describing a stratified space Σ through a 'déploiement' (unfolding). The unfolding is a tower of spaces Σ*(0)=Σ, Σ*(1), Σ*(2), …, linked by 'boundary' maps. Σ*(1) parametrises germs of strata of coniveau 1 and comes with an immersion b: Σ*(1)→Σ. On the previous page he added a second map s=p1: Σ*(1)→Σ. He required that (p1,b): Σ*(1)→Σ×Σ be injective and that its image miss the diagonal. The aim is to recover the order relation on strata (x<y) from these purely spatial data. On the previous page he abandoned an attempt to impose extra data on Σ*(2).

On this page the requirement is reformulated as a condition rather than as additional data. There should exist p2: Σ*(2)→Σ*(1) such that:
(38a) b∘p2 = s∘b', i.e. a commutative square (Σ*(2) →b' Σ*(1) →p1 Σ) = (Σ*(2) →p2 Σ*(1) →b Σ);
(38b) p1∘p2 = p1∘s'.
Such a p2 is unique, because (p1,b): Σ*(1)→Σ×Σ is a monomorphism. Its two coordinates are fixed: p1∘p2 = p1∘s' and b∘p2 = p1∘b'.

Two further requirements are imposed:
- The first square (38a) must be cartesian, i.e. Σ*(2) ≅ Σ*(1) ×_{b,Σ,p1} Σ*(1). This is a Segal-type composability condition.
- p1 must be 'transversal' to the boundary immersion b. He remarks that this is the only condition that is not purely algebraic.

He then defines (39): x<y iff there is u∈Σ*(1) with x=p1(u) and y=b(u).

On the next page he proves the order properties:
- Transitivity: given u: x<y and v: y<z, cartesianness gives a unique d∈Σ*(2) with b'(d)=v and p2(d)=u. Then w=s'(d) satisfies w: x<z. This uses (38b) and the implicit identity b∘s' = b∘b'.
- Irreflexivity: the image of (p1,b) misses the diagonal.
Hence Σ*(1) is the graph of a strict order, and Σ*(2) is the space of 2-flags x<y<z.

In modern terms: the semi-simplicial space (Σ*(n), face maps b, s, b', s', p2) is required to satisfy the Segal condition in degree 2. Together with injectivity of (p1,b) and an empty diagonal, this makes it the nerve of an internal strict poset in spaces. This is a space-level encoding of the order on strata, the input to an iterated unfolding of the stratified space into manifolds-with-corners-type pieces.
errors: Notation drifts: the same map is called s and p1, and Σ*(1) is also written Σ_*(1), Σ(1) and Σ_1. The identity b∘s' = b∘b', used on the next page, is never stated among the axioms on this page.

Transitivity needs only cartesianness of the first square plus (38b) and b∘s'=b∘b'. Neither the transversality condition nor anything topological is needed. Strictly, to get a strict order one also needs uniqueness or compatibility of composites; injectivity of (p1,b) makes this automatic. No real gap.
'Transversal' is not defined here, and the precise meaning of the condition is left vague.

ideas.what: Encoding the incidence order of strata by a tower of spaces Σ*(n) with face-type maps (b, s=p1, b', s', p2), whose degree-2 term is the fibre product Σ*(1)×_Σ Σ*(1).
ideas.modern_name: Internal poset/category in spaces via a Segal semi-simplicial object; nerve of the exit-path or stratification poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: Segal (1968, 1974) for the Segal condition; for stratified spaces, Lurie (Higher Algebra, Appendix A), Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (2014-17), Treumann (2009)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 sketches tame ('modérée') stratified spaces and their unfolding but not this axiomatics

ideas.what: The unfolding (déploiement) of a stratified space as a system of spaces of strata germs with immersions b, satisfying a cartesian (gluing) condition and a single non-algebraic transversality condition.
ideas.modern_name: Resolution or unzipping of stratified spaces into manifolds with corners / iterated fibration structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom–Mather control data; Verona; Albin–Leichtnam–Mazzeo–Piazza; Ayala–Francis–Tanaka 'unzip'
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 mentions the theme only

ideas.what: The order relation recovered via x<y iff there is u with p1 u = x and b u = y; transitivity from cartesianness; irreflexivity from the empty diagonal.
ideas.modern_name: Strict order from the Segal condition on a nerve

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates the combinatorics of strata as an internal Segal-type object in spaces: a cartesian square on germ spaces, with transversality as the only non-algebraic condition. This anticipates the AFT/Lurie viewpoint, where the poset structure of a stratification is encoded spatially (by links or unzippings) rather than by a set-theoretic poset. The explicit split between algebraic axioms and one transversality condition is a clean axiomatization not usually credited to him.
missed.quote: De plus on doit exiger que le premier carré (38) soit cartésien, et que p1 : Σ*(1) → Σ est transversal p.r. à l'immersion bordante ... (ce qui est l'unique condition de nature non purement algébrique...)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority (1981-82) for the semi-simplicial/Segal description of the unfoldings of stratified spaces, predating the ALMP and AFT resolutions. Mathematically it is routine once stated.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a nicely structured but elementary axiomatization: it amounts to the Segal condition giving a poset. Its interest is mostly historical, as an early Segal-style encoding of stratification data on spaces of strata germs. Comparable ideas exist in the later stratified-space literature.
transcription_corrections: '425 ψ' at top-left is an archival foliation mark, not mathematics.
'(s[?], p1, b) : Σ*(1) → Σ×Σ est mono' should read '(p1, b) : Σ*(1) → Σ×Σ est mono'; the first symbol is crossed out.

In the diagram, the right vertical arrow is labelled 'p1 = s' and the square is marked '(cart)'. The horizontal arrows b', b are dotted hook (immersion) arrows. The second diagram is the square Σ*(2) →s' Σ*(1) →p1 Σ and Σ*(2) →p2 Σ*(1) →p1 Σ.
